title: Conflict Repair Time Tracker
dataSources: Relationship check-ins (`relationship:checkin`), date nights (`datenight:log`), gift ideas (`giftidea:item`), keep-in-touch contacts (`keptintouch:contact`).
app: Relationship and togetherness logs — shared check-in apps, date-night and gift-idea lists, and stay-in-touch reminders — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=relationship:checkin issue_open=true resolution_hours=*
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats avg(resolution_hours) as avg_hours, perc90(resolution_hours) as p90_hours, count as issues by _time
| sort - _time
description: Measures how long it takes to repair after tension instead of just counting that tension happened.
value: A relationship with fast repair can be healthier than one with fewer but unresolved conflicts.
implementation: Log check-ins that include issue-open and resolution-hours fields; review monthly averages and tail latency.
visualization: Monthly line chart of average repair time with p90 overlay.
grandmaExplanation: It spots how long it takes to make things right after tension, because quick repair matters as much as avoiding conflict.
